result:
No. Do not add Redis here.

The system has one writer, restores from SQLite, and needs no cross-host coordination. Redis solves problems this service does not have: shared state across processes, distributed locking, cross-node caching. Adding it introduces a network hop, a second persistence model to reason about, and a new failure domain, all without addressing any current constraint.

If a need appears later, it will likely be fast in-process reads. Elixir already covers that with ETS or the process state itself, no external service required.

Revisit only if one of these changes: multiple writer processes, more than one host, or read load that SQLite measurably cannot serve.
